purpose: Batch-level harvest contracts for global microscope-slide collection survey entries. Families define common extraction behaviour; site adapters retain institution-specific URLs, terms, and promotion rules.
global_guards: Metadata first. Do not bulk-download specimen images.
Do not bypass login, anti-bot, paywall, robots, or access controls.
Preserve source wording for prepared by, mounted by, collected by, donated by, held by, digitised by, used by, received by, belonging to, and related claims.
Do not turn a collection-level count into an item-level inventory unless the source exposes item records.
Do not infer object identity from taxon, collector, or catalogue-number similarity alone.
Keep lantern slides, photographic slides, glass plate negatives, 35mm slides, plastic slides, petrographic thin sections, and microscope glass slides as distinct media/status values.

families.strategy: Fetch one authoritative institution collection page and extract collection-scale evidence only.
families.follow_links: Only same-institution links explicitly labelled collection, catalogue, database, find a specimen, inventory, or related collection.
families.stop_rule: Do not recursively crawl generic navigation or news pages.

families.strategy: Capture the authoritative collection page first, then enumerate only the linked search/gallery records that can be tied back to that collection.
families.pagination: Enumerate stable result pages or API cursors; checkpoint each page and deduplicate on institution-local item ID.
families.stop_rule: Stop when the collection filter is lost or results become generic institution-wide search hits.

families.strategy: Traverse a bounded specialist catalogue whose internal hierarchy is itself historical evidence.
families.pagination: Follow catalogue/list links on the same host; preserve parent-child hierarchy and source ordering.
families.stop_rule: Never flatten replicated published sets and unique unpublished collections into one undifferentiated item list.

families.strategy: Use official API, Darwin Core Archive, or dataset export and filter for microscope-slide preparation/material fields before creating item stubs.
families.pagination: Prefer downloadable DwC-A or documented API cursors over HTML scraping.
families.stop_rule: If the dataset does not expose a reliable slide/preparations discriminator, retain dataset-level evidence and do not claim a slide-item count.

families.strategy: Extract archival hierarchy, creators, extent, boxes/drawers, dates, former ownership, acquisition/donation language, and linked container lists.
families.follow_links: Follow only container lists, finding-aid sections, and digitised items explicitly nested under the target collection.
families.stop_rule: Do not infer number of individual slides from number of boxes or archival objects.

families.strategy: Use a paper, museum journal article, project report, legal record, institutional story, or curatorial article to establish collection existence, counts, label fields, digitisation method, conservation state, or dated collection status; keep it distinct from an official item register.
families.stop_rule: Do not promote literature table row numbers, figure numbers, programme totals, aggregate legacy counts, species counts, locality counts, or OCR artefacts into museum identifiers or slide counts.

families.strategy: Use item-page JSON or IIIF metadata endpoints when the institution explicitly exposes them; harvest metadata manifests, not image binaries.
families.pagination: Start from a bounded collection/search result and follow item records; use JSON/manifest URLs advertised by the item page.
families.stop_rule: Do not request IIIF image tiles or full-resolution derivatives in the survey workflow.

families.strategy: Keep the candidate in the survey while locating a stable catalogue, API, finding aid, or collection page. No automated harvest yet.
